source.quote: The \regret of Tsallis-INF with $\eta_t = \frac{4}{\sqrt{t}}$ and reduced variance loss estimators defined in equation \eqref{eq:rv}, in any adversarial bandit problem satisfies \[\Reg \leq 2\sqrt{(K-1)T}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{T}+14K\log(T) + \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{K} + 15.\]

results.notes: Pseudo-regret defined as E[sum l_{t,I_t}] - min_i E[sum l_{t,i}].

source.quote: Furthermore, if there exists a vector $\Delta \in [0,1]^K$ with a unique zero entry $i^*$ ... and a constant $C\geq 0$, such that the pseudo-regret at time $T$ satisfies the $(\Delta, C, T)$ self-bounding constraint ..., then the \regret additionally satisfies: $\overline{Reg}_T \leq \sum_{i\neq i*} \frac{1}{\Delta_i}((\log \frac{T(K-1)}{(\sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{1}{\Delta_i})^2}) + 6) + 28K \log(T) + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{K} + 30 + C.$

results.notes: Covers stochastic, stochastically constrained adversarial (C=0), and corrupted stochastic bandits (with C_sb = 2 x corruption).

source.label: theorem:3
source.quote: For any algorithm for an arbitrary problem domain with $K$ possible actions that satisfies $\overline{Reg}_T  \leq B \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i \neq i^* } \sqrt{\frac{\EE[w_{t,i}]}{t}} + D,$ where $B,D \geq 0$ are some constants, the \regret of the algorithm in any adversarial environment satisfies $\Reg \leq 2B\sqrt{(K-1)T} + D.$

results.notes: Meta-result for a class of algorithms in an arbitrary problem domain; mapped onto the K-armed adversarial setting. Tsallis-INF satisfies the condition with B=5/4, D=3/4 sqrt(K)+14K log T+15.
